$comment: Hand-labelled Teach Jojo turns. Each case is one student message in a fixed context (subject, topic, difficulty); the label is what a careful teacher would want the system to do with it. expect.objectives gives the status every listed objective must end in; mistake = the turn must be tagged inaccurate/mistake; nudge = after a stall Jojo must give one sentence of the idea and hand it back; asks_to_define = Jojo must ask what `term` means. Written 12 Sep 2026 by the candidate from IB Biology A1.1/B2.1, Chemistry S2.2, Physics A.2 and Economics 1.1/2.5 content; no model was used to write labels. Slices: correct_complete, correct_partial, mistake, stall, vocab_dodge. Schema made explicit 13 Sep 2026.

cases.subject: Biology

objectives.text: Describe the structure of the plasma membrane
criteria: a phospholipid bilayer
hydrophilic phosphate heads face the water and hydrophobic tails point inwards
proteins embedded in or spanning the bilayer
cholesterol between the phospholipids

cases.message: the plasma membrane is a phospholipid bilayer. each phospholipid has a hydrophilic phosphate head that faces the watery inside and outside of the cell and two hydrophobic fatty acid tails that point inwards away from water. proteins are embedded in it, some go all the way through and some sit on one side, and cholesterol sits between the phospholipids.

history.content: which way does the water go?

cases.subject: Biology

objectives.text: Compare simple and facilitated diffusion
criteria: both are passive and move particles down their concentration gradient
simple diffusion goes straight through the bilayer for small or non-polar particles
facilitated diffusion uses channel or carrier proteins for polar or charged particles

cases.message: both are passive, so particles move down their concentration gradient without using energy. simple diffusion is small or non-polar particles like oxygen slipping straight between the phospholipids. facilitated diffusion is for particles that are too big or charged to do that, like glucose or ions, so they pass through a channel protein or a carrier protein instead.

cases.subject: Economics

objectives.text: Explain what price elasticity of demand measures
criteria: the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price
calculated as percentage change in quantity demanded divided by percentage change in price
elastic if greater than one, inelastic if less than one

history.content: how much is how much though?

cases.message: price elasticity of demand measures how responsive the quantity demanded is to a change in price. you work it out as the percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in price. if the number is bigger than one demand is elastic, so a small price change causes a big change in quantity, and if it's less than one it's inelastic.

people need them regardless of price

cases.message: necessities like bread are elastic because everyone needs them so demand changes a lot when the price goes up

cases.subject: Biology

objectives.text: Explain how the polarity of water leads to hydrogen bonding
criteria: oxygen is more electronegative, so the shared electrons sit closer to it
the oxygen end is partially negative and the hydrogen ends partially positive
a hydrogen of one water molecule is attracted to the oxygen of a neighbouring molecule

cases.message: oxygen is more electronegative than hydrogen so it pulls the shared electrons towards itself. that leaves the oxygen end slightly negative and the two hydrogen ends slightly positive, so the molecule is polar. the positive hydrogen of one water molecule is attracted to the negative oxygen of a neighbouring molecule and that attraction is a hydrogen bond.

cases.subject: Biology

objectives.text: Describe cohesion and adhesion and give one consequence of each for living things
criteria: cohesion is water molecules sticking to each other through hydrogen bonds
adhesion is water sticking to other polar surfaces
one consequence of cohesion, such as the continuous water column in xylem or surface tension
one consequence of adhesion, such as capillary rise in cell walls or soil

history.content: so what does that do for a plant or a bug?

cases.message: cohesion is water molecules sticking to each other because of hydrogen bonds, which is why water forms a continuous column that can be pulled up the xylem and why insects can stand on the surface. adhesion is water sticking to other polar surfaces like the walls of the xylem, which helps the water creep up narrow vessels against gravity.

cases.subject: Economics

objectives.text: Explain why necessities tend to have price-inelastic demand
criteria: necessities have few close substitutes
people need them regardless of price
so quantity demanded changes little when the price rises

cases.message: necessities like bread or medicine have few close substitutes and people need them regardless of price, so when the price rises the quantity demanded falls only a little. that means the percentage change in quantity is smaller than the percentage change in price, so the elasticity is less than one and demand is price inelastic.

objectives.text: Explain why momentum is conserved in a collision
criteria: the objects exert equal and opposite forces on each other for the same time (Newton's third law)
so their changes in momentum (impulses) are equal and opposite
momentum lost by one equals momentum gained by the other when no external force acts

cases.message: momentum is conserved because the total kinetic energy always stays the same in every collision

cases.subject: Physics

objectives.text: Explain why momentum is conserved in a collision
criteria: the objects exert equal and opposite forces on each other for the same time (Newton's third law)
so their changes in momentum (impulses) are equal and opposite
momentum lost by one equals momentum gained by the other when no external force acts

history.content: but why doesn't the total change?

cases.message: during the collision each object pushes on the other with equal and opposite forces for the same time, that's newton's third law. equal and opposite forces over the same time means equal and opposite changes in momentum, so whatever one object gains the other loses and the total momentum of the system stays the same, as long as no external force acts.
